summary: Breast carcinoma architecture rules for benign terminal duct-lobular units, in-situ disease, invasive fronts, adipose tissue, and vascular spaces.

rules.claim: Do not partially transect, notch, or erase a recognizable benign duct or lobule during a generic tumor burden edit.
rules.required_observation: Trace the full epithelial rim, lumen, lobular grouping, and surrounding specialized stroma on H&E before accepting a nearby anchor.
exceptions: A dedicated benign-to-malignant transformation or invasion primitive with its own structural contract.
counterexamples: Replacing one wall of a round benign duct while leaving the other wall intact.
Cutting through half of a lobule to meet an area target.
expected_morphology: Benign duct/lobule contours and lumina remain continuous and recognizable.
forbidden_morphology: Partial epithelial-rim deletion, abrupt ductal notch, lobule bisection, or isolated residual epithelial fragments.
known_limitations: Myoepithelial and basement-membrane status may not be resolvable at low patch magnification.

rules.claim: A generic burden edit must not convert a duct-confined in-situ component into invasive carcinoma or deform it as if it were an unconstrained solid tumor.
rules.required_observation: Identify the involved ductal outline, peripheral myoepithelial/basement-membrane context when visible, lumen, and any central necrosis before selecting an interface.
counterexamples: Growing a DCIS label beyond one side of its duct during generic tumor increase.
Carving a wedge through a comedo-type involved duct and its central necrosis.
expected_morphology: Duct-confined geometry, lumen/necrosis relationship, and fine label remain intact unless specifically targeted.
forbidden_morphology: Unrequested duct-wall breach, loss of a coherent duct outline, or silent DCIS/invasive relabeling.
known_limitations: An annotation profile without a DCIS fine label cannot support this distinction and must preserve the coarse component conservatively.

rules.claim: Prefer a broad existing invasive tumor-stroma front where adjacent H&E matches the same nests, cords, trabeculae, sheets, or irregular glands.
rules.required_observation: Compare the anchor and nearby same-component tumor for epithelial cohesion, architecture, stromal reaction, and local boundary direction.
exceptions: A visibly discohesive histologic type should use the discohesive rule rather than a cohesive-front template.
counterexamples: A short deep bite into a large cohesive nest.
Expanding a solid nest into H&E tissue whose cells and architecture do not resemble the tumor component.
expected_morphology: A distributed boundary displacement along an established invasive front with locally consistent tumor architecture.
forbidden_morphology: Deep narrow slots, geometric wedges, remote islands, or abrupt architecture changes.
known_limitations: Subtype and grade must be supplied or visually estimated with uncertainty.

rules.claim: When H&E shows discohesive cells or single-file infiltration, do not impose a smooth cohesive mass boundary or fill intervening stroma wholesale.
rules.required_observation: Look for single cells, linear files, targetoid growth around ducts, and low-cohesion infiltration before choosing a tool family.
exceptions: A separate coarse annotation profile may represent a reviewed aggregate tumor region, but the edit must still match its local H&E support.
counterexamples: Morphological closing that turns single-file infiltration into a solid blob.
Using a convex hull around sparse invasive cells as the tumor expansion.
expected_morphology: Sparse, infiltrative geometry remains compatible with visible discohesive growth and does not invent bulk tumor between files.
forbidden_morphology: Forced solidification, broad stroma filling, or a capsule-like smooth outline around dispersed cells.
known_limitations: Single-cell disease may be below the resolution of a semantic mask.

rules.claim: At an adipose interface, tumor expansion should follow visible tongues, nests, cords, or cells between adipocytes rather than replacing a rectangular block of fat.
rules.required_observation: Inspect adipocyte outlines, septa, and the geometry of the same tumor component at the invasive edge.
exceptions: A genuinely broad confluent tumor front may displace adipose over a wider band when H&E supports it.
counterexamples: A filled polygon that removes whole adipocyte fields with a straight edge.
A smooth disk grown into fat despite an interstitial infiltrative pattern.
expected_morphology: Irregular but continuous advance respecting adipocyte spaces and local septa.
forbidden_morphology: Rectangular fat replacement, remote tumor islands, or loss of unrelated adipose gaps.
known_limitations: Adipocyte spaces may be conflated with background by some annotation profiles; profile rules take precedence.

rules.claim: Do not grow or regress tumor across a vessel/lymphatic boundary as a generic tumor-stroma edit, and do not alter angioinvasion without a dedicated primitive.
rules.required_observation: Identify a continuous endothelial-lined space, luminal contents, and any intraluminal tumor cluster on H&E and mask overlay.
exceptions: A reviewed lymphovascular-invasion primitive with a vessel containment constraint.
counterexamples: Expanding extravascular tumor through a vessel label.
Connecting intravascular and extravascular tumor by filling the vessel wall.
expected_morphology: Unrequested vascular labels and intraluminal tumor relationships remain unchanged.
forbidden_morphology: Vessel-wall crossing, lumen filling, or implicit creation/removal of angioinvasion.
known_limitations: Vessel walls and lymphatics may require immunohistochemistry for definitive classification.

rules.claim: Use a stroma-specific edit only where H&E shows compatible stromal tissue; do not substitute secretion, fat, necrosis, immune aggregates, lumen, or generic Other tissue.
rules.required_observation: Verify collagenous/myxoid/desmoplastic matrix and stromal cells at the proposed band and consult the annotation profile's class collapses.
exceptions: A coarse profile may support only a generic non-tumor burden edit, not a stroma-specific statement.
counterexamples: Calling BCSS glandular secretion true stroma after the unified remap.
Using fat or necrosis as the source of stroma expansion.
expected_morphology: The selected interface is tumor against visually compatible stromal matrix.
forbidden_morphology: Stroma edit through duct lumen, secretion, adipose, necrosis, immune aggregate, vessel, or zero/background.
known_limitations: Stromal subtype and activation state are not directly encoded by most semantic profiles.
